newsitem.title: INDIA: Copper trading seen picking up in India.
newsitem.headline: Copper trading seen picking up in India.

text.p: Business in non-ferrous metals is expected to increase further this week with local trade prices competitive against those quoted by domestic producers and imports, dealers said on Wednesday.
"The market is improving slowly, but a demand spurt is yet to come," Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh said.
Parikh said the trade was offering copper wire bar at around 13,750 rupees per quintal compared with the landed cost of imported copper wire bar at 14,800 rupees.
Prices offered by Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) were at 14,200 rupees after the state-owned domestic company raised its June price of copper wire bar by 600 rupees.
Traders could afford to offer competitive prices because of the margins they retained on imports effected when prices on the London Metals Exchange (LME) were low.
Parikh said he expected LME prices to rule firm in the next few days, strengthening local sentiment.
LME prices have a direct bearing on the domestic market as India imports most of its non-ferrous metals.
Dealers said reports of state-owned companies planning closures of unviable copper and zinc mines were disconcerting at a time when production needed to be stepped up.
Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) had decided to close down its tungsten zinc ore mines at Nagaur in northern Rajasthan state since exploration had become unviable, a company official said on Monday.
In a similar case, HCL officials said they had approached the mines ministry a couple of months ago for closure of the Mosabini mine in Bihar as it was becoming unviable.
On the Bombay metals market, activity in most metals was dull with expected demand from government agencies such as the railways and defence departments yet to materialise, dealers said.
In the week to Wednesday, tin lost 300 rupees to 30,900 rupees per quintal (100 kg) and nickel 100 rupees to 36,300.
Aluminium, zinc and lead prices were unchanged.
